claims.text: A chromium nitride coating will be applied to cast HfNbTaTiZr by physical vapor deposition.
The PVD treatment will form a chromium nitride coating on the alloy surface.
The chromium nitride coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Blocking oxygen diffusion will reduce oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
Chromium nitride coating will improve the oxygen resistance of HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
The coated alloy will maintain or improve its high-temperature yield strength relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will maintain or improve its high-temperature ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
PVD will be conducted in vacuum or inert gas.
The stated treatment or exposure duration is 1–10 hours.
Mechanical performance will be evaluated by tensile testing at 1000 °C.
The tensile strain-rate range will be 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The stated service or testing atmosphere at 1000 °C is inert gas.
Coated and uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr specimens will be compared for yield strength, ductility, and oxidation resistance.
The hypothesis will be falsified if coating significantly reduces yield strength or ductility, or fails to improve oxidation resistance.

contradictions.description: The proposed benefit is resistance to oxygen-driven oxidation, but the only specified 1000 °C atmosphere is inert gas. Such a boundary does not provide a defined oxygen-containing environment in which the oxidation-barrier claim can be decisively tested.
Exposure time is stated as 1–10 hours in the conditions but as variable in the boundary, leaving the relevant high-temperature oxidation duration unresolved.
